title: The Next Unicorns: 7 Top AI startups from the HF0 Residency
talk_summary: This is a rapid-fire pitch session from seven HF0 residency startups, mostly marketing and founder-story content with almost no engineering detail. The only transferable technical ideas are OpenRouter's model-abstraction/routing middleware and Federated AI's reliability-over-IQ framing for agents.

takeaways.technique: Homogeneous abstraction over heterogeneous model providers
takeaways.what_they_do: OpenRouter exposes one API/payment across many providers and normalizes tool calling, edge cases, and caching so switching models has near-zero cost; they also filter models by context, tool-calling, and structured-output capability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you just have a single API. You pay once and there's near zero switching costs to move from one model to another

takeaways.technique: Provider-level observability and public model rankings
takeaways.what_they_do: They track which models are used and why, and publish real-world usage rankings by category/prompt type to inform routing decisions.

takeaways.technique: Reliability-first agent design over raw model IQ
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue companies want agents that reliably complete boring tasks (forms, invoices, tickets) rather than higher-IQ models, and claim a specialized agent beats frontier models on form-filling reliability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what we actually really want is the models reliable enough to book airline tickets, sort out our emails or file taxes
takeaways.numbers: claims 99.9% reliability target vs frontier models; 'over 90% of AI projects fail'

takeaways.technique: Middleware plugins that wrap MCP and transform model output
takeaways.what_they_do: OpenRouter built 'plugins' middleware that can call MCPs internally and transform LLM outputs, sitting between the caller and the model.
